senses.definition: (now chiefly literary) A girl or an unmarried young woman.
(archaic) A female virgin.
examples: She's unmarried and still a maiden.

senses.definition: (obsolete, dialectal) A man with no experience of sex, especially because of deliberate abstention.

quotes.text: As for that ſaid ſire Bors I wille be ſhryuen with a good wylle / Soo ſyr Bors was confeſſyd / and for al wymmen ſir Bors was a vyrgyne / ſauf for one / that was the doughter of kynge Brangorys / and on her he gat a child that hyghte Elayne / and ſauf for her ſyre Bors was a clene mayden[…]
quotes.reference: 1470–1485 (date produced), Thomas Malory, “Capitulum Quartum”, in [Le Morte Darthur], book XI (in Middle English), [London: […] by William Caxton], published 31 July 1485, →OCLC, leaf 289, recto; republished as H[einrich] Oskar Sommer, editor, Le Morte Darthur […], London: David Nutt, […], 1889, →OCLC, page 577:

senses.definition: A maidservant.
A clothes maiden.
(now rare) An unmarried woman, especially an older woman.
(horse racing) A racehorse without any victory, i.e. one having a "virgin record".
(horse racing) A horse race in which all starters are maidens.
(historical) A Scottish counterpart of the guillotine.

quotes.text: It had been customary during the whole civil war, to decapitate state criminals by the instrument called the maiden; but Montrose was condemned to a more ignominious death , by a gibbet thirty feet high
quotes.reference: 1832, Robert Chambers, The History of Scotland:

senses.definition: (cricket) A maiden over.
(obsolete) A machine for washing linen.
(Wicca) Alternative form of Maiden.
Virgin.

quotes.text: It was just the middle of October when I moved in with my maiden sister […]

senses.definition: (of a female, human or animal) Without offspring.
Like or befitting a (young, unmarried) maiden.

quotes.text: Haue you no modeſty, no maiden ſhame, / No touch of baſhfulneſſe?

senses.definition: (figuratively) Being a first occurrence or event.
examples: 1975 was the year when West Indies won their maiden World Cup title.
The Titanic sank on its maiden voyage.

After Edmund Burke's maiden speech, William Pitt the Elder said Burke had "spoken in such a manner as to stop the mouths of all Europe" and that the Commons should congratulate itself on acquiring such a member.

quotes.text: Venezuelan Pastor Maldonado took his maiden victory and Williams's first since 2004 in a strategic battle with Ferrari's Fernando Alonso.

senses.definition: (cricket) Being an over in which no runs are scored.
examples: He bowled a record twelve maiden overs in his spell of 8-33 in 21 overs.

senses.definition: Fresh; innocent; unpolluted; pure; hitherto unused.

quotes.text: Come Brother Iohn, full brauely haſt thou fleſht thy Maiden ſword.
quotes.reference: c. 1597 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The First Part of Henry the Fourth, […]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene iv], page 72, column 2:

quotes.text: When I am dead, good Wench, / Let me be vs’d with Honor; ſtrew me ouer / With Maiden Flowers, that all the world may know / I was a chaſte Wife, to my Graue: Embalme me, / Then lay me forth (although vnqueen’d) yet like / A Queene, and Daughter to a King enterre me.
